entries.name: Alotau
entries.coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Alotau geo tag (town centre; a town, not an attraction)
entries.note: Town: provincial capital and gateway to Milne Bay on a natural harbour, with a waterfront, a produce and seafood market, the Turnbull WWII memorial park and the dive trade. The annual Kenu and Kundu Festival is an event, so it is not a spot (mentioned here only).
entries.reason: Kept; base passes the name test (see destinations-proposed.json name_evidence) and has the spots to fill a visit.

entries.name: Samarai
entries.note: Island: former colonial capital and trading port at the entrance to Milne Bay, a 20-minute walk round, with ruins of its boom-town past and a National Historical Heritage Island listing; reached by boat from Alotau.
entries.reason: Kept; inside the span of Alotau and reached from that base.

entries.name: Tawali
entries.note: Dive site: reef and drop-offs at Tawali on the coast near Alotau, named by the PNG tourism authority as a world-renowned Milne Bay dive site; reached by boat, with the Tawali Leisure and Dive Resort on the bluff above.
entries.reason: Kept; inside the span of Alotau and reached from that base.

entries.name: Normanby Island
entries.note: Island: unspoilt D'Entrecasteaux island with trekking trails, rainforest waterfalls and birdwatching (including the Goldie's bird-of-paradise), with very limited accommodation.
entries.reason: Kept; inside the span of Alotau and reached from that base.

entries.name: Gonubalabala
entries.pin_needed: coordinates null: needs resolve-pin.py or the owner (not guessed)
entries.note: Dive site: Gonubalabala Island waters in Milne Bay, named by the PNG tourism authority as a dive site and a known manta ray location.
entries.reason: Kept; inside the span of Alotau and reached from that base.
entries.within_span: unverified (no coordinates): described as nearby in source

entries.name: Fergusson Island
entries.note: Island: geothermal volcanic island reached only by boat, with trekking trails and birdwatching for a rare bird-of-paradise and the Curl-crested Manucode; its hot springs at Deidei are listed separately.
entries.reason: Kept; inside the span of Alotau and reached from that base.

entries.name: Trobriand Islands
entries.note: Island group: the Kiriwina Islands, raised coral atolls in the north of Milne Bay known as the Islands of Love, with yam-harvest dancing, village stays, the Kula ring and white beaches; reached by a twice-weekly PNG Air flight from Alotau.
entries.reason: Far northern Milne Bay (about 260 km from Alotau), reached by air to Kiriwina: standalone.

entries.name: Louisiade Archipelago
entries.note: Archipelago: about 100 islands in the far southeast of Milne Bay, a diver's paradise and yachting destination with coral reefs; few visitors and reached mainly by private yacht, so a region rather than a single stop.
entries.reason: Far southeast; with Misima Island and Woodlark Island only three islands, not a destination: standalone.

entries.name: Misima Island
entries.note: Island: the most populated and most accessible Louisiade island, served by air to Bwagaoia with a guest house; a closed gold mine and island-hopping stop named by the PNG tourism authority.
entries.reason: Island inside the Louisiade group; cluster below four: standalone.

entries.name: Goodenough Island
entries.note: Island: volcanic island of the D'Entrecasteaux group with rainforest, waterfalls, Mount Vineuo and good birdwatching; named as an unspoilt island to explore and a tour destination from Alotau.
entries.reason: About 100 km from Alotau, beyond 75% of any sensible span: standalone.

entries.name: Woodlark Island
entries.note: Island group: remote Woodlarks to the north of the province, known for wood carvings and coral reefs, listed as an other destination in Wikivoyage's Milne Bay guide.

reviews.name: Logea Island
reviews.reason: Rule 1: PNG tourism page names Nuli Sapi on Logea Island (one counted source); rule 2 uncertain since the draw is a resort stay, though a reef island near Samarai.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: tourism board map highlights it, easy boat ride from Alotau. Against: the named thing is a lodge (operators are not spots) and a single source.

reviews.name: Deacon's Reef
reviews.reason: Rule 1: named only in the tourism board's list of dive sites (one counted source); no coordinates, no detail.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: same source as Tawali calls it world-renowned. Against: one list mention, no pin, no description; cannot be placed without owner-supplied coordinates.

reviews.name: Wahoo Point
reviews.reason: Rule 1: only a dive-site list mention on the tourism page; no pin or detail.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: board calls it world-renowned. Against: one bare mention, nothing sourced about what is there, no coordinates.

reviews.name: Kiriwina
reviews.reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Trobriand Islands names it as the main island (airstrip, lodges, dancing). Risk of duplicating a Trobriand Islands group entry; sources describe the group as one visitor area.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: the island where all visitors land. Against: near-duplicate of the group entry; dancing is tied to a yam festival (event). Keep only one of Kiriwina or the group.

reviews.name: Dobu Island
reviews.reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Milne Bay names it as a most significant small island with volcanic activity (inline in Other destinations, not its own listing); one source.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: counted source plus 3,097 views, volcanic. Against: no listing of its own, no visitor facilities, little to do.

note: PNG has no existing destinations or spots. Placement run jointly for all nine regions; proposed destinations are in curation/png/destinations-proposed.json.
